sections.heading: SEO and AI search in Orange
sections.body_html:
The City of Orange, about three miles north of Santa Ana, had 139,911 residents in 2020. Wikipedia notes it is unusual in the region because many homes in its Old Towne district were built before 1920 and were preserved when other cities demolished theirs, and the small city of Villa Park is surrounded by Orange.

Downtown Orange hosts the Orange International Street Fair every Labor Day weekend, held since 1973 and drawing an average of 400,000 people. The city also has the Orange County Zoo in Irvine Regional Park and shopping at The Village at Orange and The Outlets at Orange.

sections.heading: How Orange customers search
sections.body_html:
Searches in Orange split between visitors exploring Old Towne's shops, antiques and restaurants, and residents looking for everyday services, healthcare and home improvement.

Because the city shares its name with the county, people often search for things like 'dentist in Orange' and mean the city. Clear address details and the words City of Orange or Old Towne help search engines and AI understand where you are.

sections.heading: How Google ranks local results in Orange
sections.body_html:
Google publishes the basics of how local results work. According to its Business Profile help, results are mainly based on relevance, distance and popularity. Prominence, in Google's words, is how well-known a business is, which draws on links from other websites and on reviews, and more reviews and positive ratings can help. Google also states plainly that nobody can request or pay for a better local ranking.

The shared name makes relevance tricky: Google has to work out whether a search means the city or the county. Precise location details, a correctly placed map pin and reviews that mention Old Towne or the neighborhood help.

sections.heading: Getting recommended by ChatGPT and Google AI in Orange
sections.body_html:
AI assistants need unambiguous details. Pages that say City of Orange, California, with a street address and nearby landmarks, are easier for them to match to local questions.

Ask these questions in ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google each month and record who is named:

  1. Where are the best antique shops in Old Towne Orange?
  2. Which restaurant near the Orange Plaza is good for brunch?
  3. Who is a good contractor for a historic home in Orange?
  4. Which pediatric dentist in Orange, CA has good reviews?
  5. What should I do at the Orange International Street Fair?

sections.heading: Business Profile basics
sections.body_html:
Your Google Business Profile is usually the first thing people see in a local search.

If you work at customers' homes, Google's guidelines treat you as a service-area business: one profile for your central office or location, with a service area set. Virtual offices, meaning rented addresses you do not work from, are not eligible, and neither are P.O. boxes. Use your real-world business name, the one on your signage and invoices, with no added keywords.

sections.heading: Reviews
sections.body_html:
Ask customers to mention what they bought or what you fixed. For historic-home trades, reviews describing the type of house add credibility.

Stay inside Google's rules. Its Maps content policy bans fake engagement and says reviews must come from genuine experiences. Offering payment, discounts or free services for a review, or for removing a bad one, is not allowed. The safe method is simple: ask every real customer, send a direct review link and reply to what people write.

sections.heading: Structured data
sections.body_html: Add LocalBusiness structured data, or the most specific Schema.org type for your business, with your real name, address, phone, hours and service area, matching your Business Profile exactly. Google's local business documentation explains how this markup can help it show your details.

sections.heading: City pages that help Orange customers
sections.body_html:
An Orange page is useful when it describes real local work, such as restoring historic Old Towne homes or serving shoppers around the Plaza.

Be careful with city pages. Google's spam policies call pages aimed at specific regions or cities that funnel users to one page, and substantially similar pages, doorway abuse. A city page earns its place only with genuinely local detail, such as real projects, local rules or response times there.

sections.heading: How to choose an SEO company
sections.body_html:

  • Ask how often you get reports.
